note: Original brewing explanations informed by the linked producer references. Flavor expectations are guidance, not measured outcomes. App notes describe BrewMaster's own model.

profiles.label: Kettle bittering
profiles.summary: Boil additions mainly used to reach your bitterness target.
profiles.when: Added to the kettle during the boil, commonly early enough for a longer boil contact. Recipe minutes mean time remaining before the boil ends.
profiles.effect: Heat turns hop alpha acids into bitter compounds. Alpha-acid percentage, amount and boil time influence the IBU estimate. Longer boiling changes how much hop aroma remains.
profiles.app: The app favors higher-alpha candidates for this use and adjusts kettle amounts toward your IBU target. You can override the variety, amount and timing.

source.title: Yakima Chief Hops · whole-leaf brewing uses

profiles.label: Late-boil flavor
profiles.summary: A hop addition near the end of the boil to add hop character along with some bitterness.
profiles.when: Added during the last part of the boil. A 10-minute addition means 10 minutes before the boil ends.
profiles.effect: A shorter boil contact can retain more aroma character than an early addition while still adding bitterness. Results depend on the hop, dose and process.
profiles.app: The app ranks boil-use flavor evidence and starts this addition at up to 10 minutes. Recipe search may adjust its amount and timing, and you can edit the result.

profiles.label: Whirlpool aroma
profiles.summary: A hot hop steep after the boil, aimed at hop aroma and flavor.
profiles.when: Added after boiling stops, while the wort (unfermented beer) is still hot and before it is fully cooled. This is also called a hop stand.
profiles.effect: Temperature and contact time shape aroma and can also add bitterness. A whirlpool addition can help build hop character while keeping kettle bitterness under control.
profiles.app: The app ranks descriptor evidence for whirlpool use. Its bitterness estimate uses your reduced whirlpool utilization setting; amount, stand time and that setting remain editable.

profiles.label: Dry hopping
profiles.summary: Hops added to cooled beer during or after fermentation, primarily to build aroma.
profiles.when: Added in the fermenter during active fermentation or after it finishes. Record contact time in days in the recipe editor.
profiles.effect: Hop variety, dose and fermentation stage influence the aroma. Strong hop aroma can coexist with a low calculated IBU; perceived bitterness can still change.
profiles.app: The app uses dry-hop descriptor evidence and treats dry hops as zero IBU in its calculation. That is a model assumption, not a guarantee of zero perceived bitterness. Amount and contact time are editable.
